title: A root-cause, durable treatment for ADPKD

concept.text: The innovation would be a safe, durable treatment for autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) that corrects its disease-driving genetic defect or restores enough polycystin function to prevent or arrest progressive cyst formation and kidney damage. Genetic correction is one possible route; a pathway-directed intervention could also qualify if it durably addresses the underlying functional defect. The supplied experimental evidence directly tests base editing, rather than establishing these alternative approaches.

The intended achievement extends beyond correcting one mutation in an experimental model. It requires effective treatment of enough relevant kidney cells, coverage of a clinically meaningful range of disease-causing variants, and sustained benefit without unacceptable toxicity. Preventing new damage, arresting existing disease, rebuilding scarred tissue, and treating disease outside the kidney are distinct capabilities; success in one does not establish the others.

significance.text: If sufficient polycystin function could be restored safely and durably in humans, treatment could interrupt an inherited cause of cystic kidney disease before it produces progressive organ damage. The mouse results provide a technical basis for that possibility: partial correction of a pathogenic variant was associated with restoration of mature polycystin-1, reduced cyst growth, and improved renal markers. Preventing kidney failure in a broad patient population remains a prospective human benefit.

As a conditional downstream consequence, preventing substantial loss of kidney function could reduce the need for dialysis or transplantation and the burden of repeated treatment. The scale of that benefit would depend on when treatment becomes effective, how many patients and variants it can cover, how long protection lasts, and whether it is practical to deliver. The supplied evidence does not establish a population-level benefit estimate.

Correcting the initiating defect should not be equated with regenerating a damaged organ. Reduced fibrosis after early treatment does not demonstrate reconstruction of previously scarred kidneys. Renal benefit also does not establish control of all manifestations outside the kidney: the kidney-directed mouse treatment did not normalize the reported heart-weight-to-body-weight ratio or cardiac hypertrophy, whereas the broadly expressed construct showed cardiac benefits. Broader treatment or separate interventions may therefore be needed, but their necessity has not been established.

missing_breakthrough.text: The central unsolved capability is durable, clinically useful restoration of polycystin function in human kidneys with an acceptable safety profile. ADPKD involves multiple disease-associated genes and variant classes. A base editor designed for one pathogenic nucleotide change cannot by itself establish coverage of that diversity. Different variants may require different editors or other ways of restoring function, and the supplied evidence does not determine which strategy would provide sufficiently broad coverage.

Delivery remains a concrete engineering barrier. Treatment must reach enough disease-relevant kidney cells and produce enough functional correction to alter disease progression. The study achieved partial renal editing using a dual-vector AAV system; its discussion identifies the high AAV doses needed for efficient kidney targeting as a safety concern. Kidney-directed expression also did not mean exclusively renal activity, because the article reported liver effects.

Durability must be assessed together with safety. Prolonged expression of Cas9 and the deaminase may increase off-target editing risks and provoke immune responses, particularly when moving to larger animals and humans. Limited mouse follow-up cannot establish lifelong human benefit or safety. A permanent DNA correction and persistent delivery of editing machinery are different properties; the latter introduces risks that must be evaluated alongside the intended correction.

Advanced disease presents an additional biological challenge. Progressive fibrosis and declining kidney function may leave damage that genetic correction alone does not repair. A claim of reversal would need evidence of recovery from established structural injury, including the consequences of existing cysts and scarring. The pathology makes this a reasonable additional requirement, rather than proof that restoration is impossible.

current_state.text: Cheng and colleagues published “In vivo base editing rescues ADPKD in a humanized mouse model” in Nature Communications on December 11, 2025. The study used AAV9-delivered ABE9 base-editing systems to target the R3277C variant in humanized Pkd1 mice. It examined both RC/RC and RC/null genotypes, which share the targeted variant; these are two model genotypes, not evidence of broad coverage across different pathogenic variants.

The kidney-directed Ksp construct, administered on postnatal day 14, produced partial renal correction and delayed cyst growth. The article text reports renal DNA editing of 23.4 ± 0.4%, together with a reduced cystic index and improved renal dysfunction markers. That percentage describes the reported renal DNA measurement; it does not establish the fraction of every relevant cell type corrected or a threshold sufficient for human treatment. The study also reported less fibrosis after early intervention, which does not demonstrate reversal of previously established scarring.

The broadly expressed Cbh construct provided complementary evidence that a single administered dose could delay cyst growth through partial correction of the RC variant and restoration of polycystin-1 expression. Differences between the broadly expressed and kidney-directed constructs, including their cardiac outcomes, show that expression pattern affects the scope of benefit. These findings demonstrate mouse proof of principle; they do not demonstrate a human cure, lifelong durability, or restoration of advanced human kidneys.

The supplied review assessed a retained full article text and figure captions. Figure images, supplementary files, and underlying data were not supplied for inspection, so the account above relies on the textual findings documented in that review rather than independent examination of those materials. The source index records a nontruncated HTML extraction without reported extraction issues, but that does not remove the limits on the materials reviewed.

The supplied freshness record for the assessment as of November 1, 2026 is empty. Consequently, these inputs support an account of the December 2025 publication but do not establish whether later work changed the field's position. This gap does not invalidate the reported mouse findings or establish that subsequent progress has or has not occurred.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: show in humans that a genetic or pathway-directed intervention safely restores sufficient polycystin function, substantially prevents or arrests cyst growth, and preserves kidney function and patient outcomes over extended follow-up. A convincing program would connect the intervention's biological effect to structural and clinical benefit, rather than relying on an editing percentage alone. These are proposed criteria, not established consensus standards.
completion_criteria.label: Polycystin restoration safely sustains human cyst control and kidney outcomes

completion_criteria.text: Proposed breadth and reproducibility requirements: define the eligible genes, variants, disease stages, and patient groups in advance, and reproduce benefit across a clinically meaningful range within that scope. Confirmation in independent studies and across treatment batches would strengthen confidence that outcomes are reliable. Finite studies can establish demonstrated breadth within tested populations; they cannot establish literal applicability to every ADPKD variant or patient.
completion_criteria.label: Benefit reproduces across a predefined, clinically meaningful ADPKD scope

completion_criteria.text: Proposed safety and practical requirements: establish a feasible delivery method and dose, quantify kidney targeting and unintended exposure elsewhere, and assess off-target changes, immune responses, and consequences of persistent editor expression. Follow-up should be long enough to evaluate both sustained benefit and delayed harms. A clinical protocol would need to specify meaningful effect sizes, follow-up duration, and whether repeat dosing is necessary and feasible; the supplied evidence does not resolve those choices.
completion_criteria.label: Feasible delivery sustains benefit with quantified long-term safety

completion_criteria.text: Proposed boundaries for stronger claims: advanced-disease reversal should require recovery of architecture and function in kidneys with documented pre-existing injury. Less damage after early treatment would support prevention or arrest, without satisfying that reversal claim. Claims of systemic ADPKD treatment should separately demonstrate benefit for relevant manifestations outside the kidney.
completion_criteria.label: Stronger: Demonstrate injured-kidney recovery and benefits beyond the kidney

related_concepts.text: NEP-01, “Regrow functional nephrons inside an adult human kidney,” and NEP-02, “Rebuild function in scarred kidneys by reversing established fibrosis,” address restoration capabilities that could complement NEP-08 in advanced disease. Preventing polycystin-driven cyst formation does not demonstrate new nephron formation or reversal of established fibrosis. These remain distinct innovations even if a future treatment combines them.

NEP-03, “Manufacture transplantable human kidneys from cells,” NEP-04, “A durable, implantable artificial kidney,” NEP-05, “Kidney replacement that is portable and affordable at global scale,” and NEP-06, “An effectively unlimited supply of durable animal-donor kidneys,” concern replacing lost kidney function or supplying replacement organs. NEP-08 aims to preserve the patient's own kidneys by addressing ADPKD's cause. Successful prevention could reduce demand for replacement, while replacement would remain relevant for patients whose damage cannot be sufficiently arrested or repaired.

NEP-07, “Reliably induce donor-specific tolerance in kidney recipients,” addresses immune acceptance of a transplanted kidney. It could benefit people with ADPKD who need transplantation, but correcting a defect in a patient's own kidney cells does not establish donor-specific transplant tolerance. Immune responses to a gene-delivery vector or editing machinery are a separate problem from tolerance to a donor organ.

NEP-09, “Durable reversal of diabetic kidney disease,” shares the goal of sustained disease modification but concerns a different disease mechanism and requires its own evidence of reversal. NEP-10, “Broad prevention of severe acute kidney injury,” concerns prevention of acute injury across its stated scope. Success against an inherited polycystin defect would not establish either diabetic disease reversal or broad protection against acute kidney injury.

change_log.change: Expanded the concept to distinguish variant correction, functional polycystin restoration, prevention or arrest, advanced structural repair, and treatment outside the kidney.
change_log.reason: The review identifies these as separate scientific achievements that should not be conflated.

change_log.change: Added the publication date, AAV9/ABE9 delivery system, R3277C target, RC/RC and RC/null model scope, early treatment timing, and reported 23.4 ± 0.4% renal DNA editing.
change_log.reason: These review-supported details make the demonstrated achievement concrete while preserving its single-variant, preclinical limits.

change_log.change: Clarified that reduced fibrosis following early treatment does not establish regeneration of previously scarred kidneys.
change_log.reason: Prevention of damage and reversal of established injury require different evidence.

change_log.change: Qualified kidney-directed delivery and systemic benefit using reported liver effects and differences in cardiac outcomes between constructs.
change_log.reason: Kidney-directed expression is not exclusive renal activity, and separate interventions for extrarenal disease remain a possibility rather than an established necessity.

change_log.change: Integrated delivery dose, persistent editor expression, off-target editing, and immune-response barriers.
change_log.reason: These are concrete translational limitations documented in the supplied review.

change_log.change: Retained conditional human significance while separating it from demonstrated mouse outcomes.
change_log.reason: The evidence supports a technical basis for the innovation without establishing human efficacy, lifelong durability, or broad variant coverage.

change_log.change: Expanded completion criteria into explicitly proposed demonstrations with defined scope and reproducibility requirements.
change_log.reason: The original criteria require operational definition, and finite testing cannot establish universal applicability.

change_log.change: Preserved review-access limitations and the unresolved freshness assessment.
change_log.reason: Full article text availability does not imply inspection of figures, supplements, or underlying data, and an empty freshness record cannot establish later progress.

change_log.change: Explained relationships to every other supplied roster entry without merging their identities.
change_log.reason: Disease correction, regeneration, organ replacement, transplant tolerance, and prevention of other kidney diseases have overlapping goals but distinct completion requirements.

unresolved_issues: Whether later research changed the field after the December 2025 study remains unresolved because the supplied freshness record is empty.
The fraction and distribution of relevant human kidney cells that must regain sufficient polycystin function for durable clinical benefit are not established by these inputs.
The appropriate strategy and achievable coverage across different ADPKD genes and variant classes remain unresolved.
Human delivery feasibility, acceptable dose, long-term safety, durability, and repeat-dosing requirements remain unestablished in the supplied evidence.
The potential for correction alone to repair established cystic architecture and fibrosis, and the need for additional regenerative interventions, remain open.
The scope of extrarenal benefit and whether broader delivery or separate treatments would be required remain unresolved.
Clinical effect sizes, variant coverage targets, and follow-up durations for the proposed completion criteria require future protocol definition.
Figure images, supplementary materials, and underlying data were not available to the supplied review, limiting independent assessment beyond the retained article text and captions.
